title: Chatham-Kent OPP officer charged in shooting death of man
subtitle: A Chatham-Kent OPP officer has been charged with manslaughter and criminal negligence after a 24-year-old man was shot and killed last summer.
article: A Chatham-Kent OPP officer has been charged with manslaughter and criminal negligence after a 24-year-old man was shot and killed last summer.
According to a Friday release from the province's police watchdog, there were "reasonable grounds" to lay criminal charges in the July 7 incident.

"The Chatham-Kent OPP responded to a call about a gasoline theft. Officers located the vehicle believed to be involved travelling westbound on Highway 401 and followed it," the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) stated.
"The vehicle ended up in the ditch dividing the highway. One of the officers approached the vehicle, and his firearm discharged and shot the driver. The man died in hospital."
As a result of the SIU investigation, Const. Sean O'Rourke is charged with one count of manslaughter and one count of criminal negligence causing death.
O'Rourke was arrested Friday by members of the SIU before being released on an undertaking with conditions.
He is required to appear before the Ontario court of justice in Chatham on Feb. 16.
"As the matter is before the courts, and in consideration of the fair trial interests of the accused, the SIU will not provide further comment on the investigation," the SIU added.
The SIU is an independent government agency that investigates incidents involving police that may have resulted in death, serious injury, sexual assault and/or the discharge of a firearm at a person.
